annotation.title_clean: Humanitarian benefits of emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapon systems
annotation.title_en: Humanitarian benefits of emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapon systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United States of America (submission to CCW Group of Governmental Experts)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS, CCW/GGE.1/2018/WP.4
annotation.summary_en: US working paper to the 2018 CCW GGE on lethal autonomous weapons, arguing that autonomy and AI in weapons can reduce civilian casualties. Examples include self-destruct mechanisms, AI-aided situational awareness, collateral damage estimation, automated targeting and defensive autonomous systems. It urges States to encourage such innovation rather than stigmatize or ban LAWS.
key_provisions_or_claims: Autonomous self-destruct/self-deactivation mechanisms reduce unintended harm to civilians
AI can increase commanders' awareness of civilians and improve collateral damage assessments
Automated target identification, tracking and engagement improves precision and reduces collateral damage
Robotic and defensive autonomous systems reduce need for immediate self-defense fires
States should encourage rather than stigmatize or ban emerging LAWS technologies
